lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Deep Space Whalesong. Lane twelve. All is well.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: This is Captain Hum. Deep Space Whalesong. Rest easy.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Deep Space Whalesong, night watch. The whales are fine.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Ninety-nine point six. Deep Space Whalesong. Somewhere between galaxies.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Whalesong.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Carry on.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Captain's log. We are drifting at a comfortable speed. One galaxy per century. No rush.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales are swimming alongside. They are fine. I asked.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Well. I didn't ask. You don't ask the whales.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: If you can't sleep, that's alright. The ship is awake. The whales are awake.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Someone is always awake out here. You're in good company.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: One of the whales turned and looked at the ship just now. For quite a long time.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I'm sure it's nothing.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Carry on.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: It's very dark out here tonight. That's normal. It's always dark out here.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I just like to mention it, so you know that I've noticed.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Odd sighting off the port side. A small flock of geese. In space. Flying in formation.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: They looked at us as if we owed them something.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We don't. I don't think we do.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Good morning. There is no morning out here, of course. But I keep one for you anyway.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Here it is. Good morning.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We have a stowaway. A shadow, sitting very quietly in the observation lounge. Says his name is Greg. Says he wanted to see the whales.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Well. Who doesn't.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales are singing again. Long, low notes. They carry for light years.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Somewhere a very long way from here, someone is hearing this, and they don't know why they feel better.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: That's the whales.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I'll leave you now. I'll be back in an hour or so. Maybe two.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales will keep you company. Don't ask them anything. Just listen.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Faint signal on the long-range set. A man called Teodor, at Relay Four, asking if anyone can hear him.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We can, Teodor. So can the whales. They've started singing back.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The Night Watch. Deep Space Whalesong.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I'm on watch. You can sleep.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Night watch report. All quiet in lane twelve.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales are singing to each other. One of them has been answering a question for three hundred years.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: She's nearly at the good bit.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I checked on the whales just now.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: From a distance. Through the glass. You don't knock on the whales.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: They're fine.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Good morning. There is no morning out here.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: This is the Dawn Log. I keep one anyway.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Captain's log. Dawn, by my reckoning.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I've turned the lights in the observation lounge up a little, and made a pot of coffee. That's how you make a dawn out here.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: It works. Mostly.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Good morning to the night shift, on whatever ship you're keeping.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: It's been a long night. You did well. Here's a slow one.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Captain Hum.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Still on watch.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Deep Space Whalesong.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: All is well.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: It's very dark out here.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: That's normal.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Pod Seven passed the ship an hour ago. Seven whales in a line, singing the same note.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: It went on for a long time. The coffee went cold. I didn't mind.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We've drifted past another galaxy. It was very beautiful. It took most of the century.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I waved. I don't think it noticed.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: One of the whales has started humming along with our music.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I don't know which one. I'm not going to ask.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: You don't ask the whales.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The Nebula Choir have gone quiet for a while. They do that. They're listening to something we can't hear.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I like to think it's us.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Ship's systems, all green. Coffee, warm. Whales, fine.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: That's the whole report. It's a good report.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Sleep easy.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Carry on.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I'll leave you with the whales now.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Here's some more drift. No rush.

clips.title: Greg Comes Home, Part One: The Stowaway Decides

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Captain's log. The stowaway in the observation lounge has asked to speak to me.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: His name is Greg. He's a shadow. He came aboard in the spring, to see the whales. He has seen a great many whales.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Captain. I'd like to get off.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We're between galaxies, son. There isn't really an off.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I know. Sorry. It's just. One of the whales turned and looked at me today. For a very long time.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: They do that. I'm sure it was nothing.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: The others told me. She sings, and it takes a thousand years for anyone to hear it. And then a thousand more before anyone sings back.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I don't want him to wait a thousand years.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Who?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Hollis. My person. I left without saying anything. He leaves the porch light on.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Well.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: There's a comet coming through lane twelve tonight, heading back toward the inner dimensions. It has a beach on it. Stand by the airlock at four, and you could hop across.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Will you slow down for me?

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Son, we go one galaxy a century. We're already slowed down.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: And Greg. The whale who looked at you. She wasn't singing to you.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: She was singing you home.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Captain's log, continued. The stowaway has left the ship. The whales are fine. I didn't ask. I could tell.

clips.title: Teodor Is Heard, Part Five: Some Rush

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Captain's log. A faint signal on the long-range set, as there has been every night for eleven years. A man called Teodor, at Relay Four, asking if anyone can hear him.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales have been singing back to him since the first night. But his receiver is broken, and whale song travels slowly.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I've done the sums. At the speed of whale, their answer reaches him in nine hundred and eighty nine years.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: That's too long.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: This ship goes one galaxy a century. It always has. There's never been any rush out here.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: There is now.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I've asked the whales to come in close, and sing into the hull, so we can carry it for them. It's the first time I've ever asked the whales anything.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: They sang one long, low note. I'm choosing to take that as yes.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We're turning toward the edge of the dial. Two galaxies a century. Possibly three.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Hold on to your coffee. And Teodor, hold on. Help is coming. It's very large and very slow, but it's coming faster than it ever has.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Captain's log. Halloween, by my reckoning.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: One of the whales swam past with a sheet of nebula draped over her head. I think she's dressed as a ghost.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I said boo. She said nothing.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: You don't say boo to the whales.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Deep Space Whalesong. Halloween night watch.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Nothing out here is scary. Except how big it all is.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Ship's log. A moon has gone missing, they say. Nobody can agree which.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We passed a great many moons tonight. I didn't count them. I will now.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales are fine.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Ship's log. A smell of toast, in the observation lounge, and, I'm told, everywhere else.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We have no toaster aboard.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales are fine.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales are singing a song I've heard somewhere before.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: They stop at the same place every time. Then they start again.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I think they're waiting for somebody to finish it.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Three knocks on the hull.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: We are between galaxies. There is nobody out there.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I said come in, anyway. It seemed polite.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The nebula off the port side went a colour just now. I've no word for it.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: The whales went very quiet. Then they sang it.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Carry on.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Ship's log. A pigeon is walking along the bridge.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: I don't know how it came aboard. It seems to know the ship. It went straight to the coffee.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Carry on.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Ship's log. The relay ships are drifting. Two passed us this week, well off their lanes.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: Past one hundred and eight, there's music I don't know. The whales have started singing back.

lines.speaker: Captain Hum
lines.text: They're fine.
